title: LegosTracker: LEGO sets as a market

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Would a LEGO set from 1965 have been a good investment? Antoine's project treats LEGO as a market to find out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ha. Where does the data come from?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two places. The Rebrickable catalog says which sets, parts and themes exist, and a scraper adds the prices sets fetch over time from BrickEconomy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It reads a list of set numbers, drives a visible Chromium window with Playwright, and opens each set's page. It pulls the chart data out of the page and saves value history and price bands as CSV files, plus details like pricing and predictions into one table.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And then the data science part?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Notebooks explore the catalog, then fit regressions on the price history of set zero zero one dash one, project it to 2030 and run a Monte Carlo simulation. Another notebook updates the values of your own collection.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's for collectors and data curious people. The article on the blog tells the story with charts.
